I am a Senior Lecturer in Health Economics at Newcastle Business School, the
University of Newcastle, Australia.

My PhD in Economics is from Ca' Foscari University of Venice, where I used stated
preference methods to study how people make healthcare decisions. Before that I
took an MSc in Health Economics and Management at the University of Bologna, an
MSc in Economics at Addis Ababa University, and a BA in Economics at Jimma
University. I was a postdoctoral fellow at Ca' Foscari, then a Research Fellow at the Health
Economics Research Unit in Aberdeen, a postdoctoral fellow at the Harrison School
of Pharmacy at Auburn, and a Health Measurement and Regulatory Science Fellow at
Duke University School of Medicine. I joined Newcastle as a Lecturer in 2023 and
have been a Senior Lecturer since 2026.

The through-line is preference measurement: what people are willing to trade, how
reliably we can measure it, and what happens to the measurement when the person
answering has not read everything we put in front of them. The last of those is
why I use eye tracking, and why a fair amount of my work is about method rather
than about any one clinical question.

I also build things. Estimates that stay in a paper reach a narrow audience;
estimates in a working tool reach whoever has the decision. Three of those tools
are [public](/tools/).

## Service

Guest Editor, *Health Policy and Technology*. Reviewer for the *Journal of Health
Economics*, *Health Economics*, *Value in Health*, *Social Science & Medicine*, the
*Journal of Choice Modelling*, *Theory and Decision*, and *BMJ Open*.

I coordinate health economics and preference research activity at Newcastle and
work with early-career researchers across the group.
